Admonished for calling himself most learned, Moses sought Khadir but could not stay patient as Khadir holed a boat, killed a boy and repaired a wall.
Asked whether fighting from anger or pride is in Allah's cause, the Prophet said only one who fights so that Allah's word is highest fights in Allah's cause.
Near the Jamra people asked about Hajj rites done out of order, and the Prophet told each to do it now, for there is no harm.
When some Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit, he fell silent as if inspired, then recited that its knowledge is with his Lord and people have little knowledge.
The Prophet told Aisha that, but for her people being newly out of ignorance, he would rebuild the Ka'bah with an entrance and an exit door, which Ibn Az-Zubair did.
The Prophet told Mu'adh that whoever sincerely testifies to Allah's oneness and his messengership is saved from Hell, but not to spread it lest people depend on it.
Um Sulaim asked whether a woman must bathe after a wet dream, and the Prophet said yes if she sees discharge, which explains why a child resembles its mother.
Ibn Umar was too shy to name the date palm when the Prophet asked which tree is like a Muslim, and his father wished he had answered.
Too shy to ask himself, Ali had Al-Miqdad ask about frequent urethral discharge, and the Prophet said it requires ablution.
The Prophet named where the people of Medina, Syria, Najd and perhaps Yemen assume ihram, and said a muhrim avoids shirts, turbans, trousers, hooded cloaks and scented garments.
Prayer after hadath needs ablution, whose traces will make the Prophet's followers shine on Resurrection Day, and one who doubts in prayer leaves only on hearing or smelling something.
The Prophet prayed after sleeping without new ablution, made a light ablution after Arafat and a full one at Muzdalifa, and Ibn Abbas demonstrated his ablution handful by handful.
A man who asks Allah's protection from Satan, in Allah's name, before intercourse with his wife will have any child destined from it safe from Satan's harm.
The Prophet sought refuge on entering the toilet, prayed for Ibn Abbas for bringing water, and forbade facing the Qibla in the open, though Ibn Umar saw him face Jerusalem.
The Prophet's wives went out at night to relieve themselves; Umar, wanting them veiled, called out to Sauda, Allah revealed the veil verses, and the Prophet let them go out.
Ibn Umar saw the Prophet relieving himself facing Syria with his back to the Qibla, and Anas and another boy followed him carrying water for cleaning and a short spear.
One should not touch or clean the private parts with the right hand nor breathe into a drinking vessel, and the Prophet cleaned himself with stones, rejecting bone and dung.
The Prophet washed the limbs once or twice, and Uthman, washing thrice, reported that such an ablution followed by an attentive prayer brings forgiveness of sins.
Ablution includes rinsing the nose and, after sleep, washing the hands before dipping them; stones are used in odd numbers, and unwashed heels are threatened with the Fire.
Ibn Umar explained four habits others noticed, touching only the Yemeni corners, wearing tanned shoes, dyeing with henna and delaying ihram, as following what he saw the Prophet do.
When his daughter died the Prophet told those washing her to begin on the right with the parts washed in ablution.
The Prophet liked to begin with the right side in putting on shoes, combing his hair, washing himself and everything else.
When no water could be found for the Asr ablution, the Prophet put his hand in a pot and water sprang from between his fingers until all had made ablution.
Abida said one hair of the Prophet would be dearer to him than the world, and Abu Talha took the first of his hair when his head was shaved.
A vessel a dog drinks from is washed seven times, a man entered Paradise for watering a thirsty dog, and no water was sprinkled where dogs urinated in the mosques.
Game caught by one's trained dog sent with Allah's name may be eaten, unless the dog ate from it or another dog joined the hunt.
Waiting in the mosque counts as prayer until hadath, doubt requires a sound or smell, and urethral discharge and intercourse without emission were each said to need ablution.
Usama poured water for the Prophet's ablution after Arafat, and Al-Mughira on a journey, when he wiped over his head and khuffs.
Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas saw the Prophet wake at midnight, recite the last ten verses of Al-Imran, make ablution and pray two rak'at six times and a witr.
After a solar eclipse prayer the Prophet said he had seen Paradise and Hell, and that in the grave people will be asked about him: believers answer, hypocrites cannot.
Asked to show the Prophet's ablution, Abdullah bin Zaid rinsed mouth and nose and washed his face thrice, forearms twice, wiped his head back and forth, and washed his feet.
People wiped themselves with the Prophet's leftover ablution water, he had Abu Musa and Bilal drink and pour from his tumbler, and companions nearly fought over such water.
As-Sa'ib's aunt brought him ill to the Prophet, who prayed for him; he drank the leftover ablution water and saw the seal of prophethood between the Prophet's shoulders.
Abdullah bin Zaid again showed the Prophet's ablution from a pot, and Ibn Umar said men and women made ablution together in the Prophet's lifetime.
The Prophet visited the unconscious Jabir and sprinkled his ablution water on him; Jabir woke and asked who would inherit from him, and the verses on inheritance were revealed.
Water in a small painted pot brought to the Prophet sufficed for the ablution of eighty or more people.
The Prophet washed his hands and face in a tumbler and threw in a mouthful, and made ablution from a brass pot, washing his face thrice and forearms twice.
When his illness grew severe the Prophet was nursed in Aisha's house with his wives' consent and had seven skins of water poured over him before going to the people.
Asked by a man who used too much water, Abdullah bin Zaid showed the Prophet's ablution from an earthenware pot, rinsing mouth and nose thrice from one handful.
Water sprang from between the Prophet's fingers in a shallow tumbler, enough for seventy to eighty people to make ablution.
